findings.title: Serial googleOrganicTaskGetAdvanced awaits inside poll loop — N ready tasks per tick = N sequential RTTs
findings.suggested_fix: Collect all matching ready task IDs from readyItems (filter at line 189), then await Promise.allSettled(ids.map(fetchAndEmit)) instead of the for loop. Add p-limit at 10-20 to avoid DataForSEO rate limits. Node.js single-threaded event loop makes events.push and retrieved.add safe from concurrent async tasks.
findings.why_it_matters: At 210 tasks completing between ticks (typical first-tick catchup at t=30s), 210 sequential awaits at ~200ms RTT adds ~42s of serial fetch time per tick before the poll loop proceeds. This consumes a significant fraction of the 10-minute ceiling and delays downstream event processing proportionally to run size.
evidence: Line 187: for (const readyItem of readyItems) — synchronous iteration over all ready items.
Line 192: const taskRes = await api.googleOrganicTaskGetAdvanced(taskId) — awaited serially inside the loop, blocking all subsequent tasks until each fetch completes.
Typical run: 210 tasks; DEFAULT_POLL_INITIAL_MS=30000 means all tasks likely complete before first tick, so first tick serially fetches all 210.

findings.title: Sequential chunk POST loop — 3 chunks POSTed serially, wastes ~2 RTTs at typical scale
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the for loop (line 147) with: const chunkResults = await Promise.all(chunks.map(chunk => api.googleOrganicTaskPost(chunk.map(buildTask)))); then iterate chunkResults to populate taskIdToQuery.
findings.why_it_matters: 3 serial POST round trips add ~400-600ms of unnecessary startup latency before polling begins. Impact is small at stated scale (3 batches) but grows linearly with inputs.length / CHUNK_SIZE.
evidence: Line 147: for (const chunk of chunks) — serial iteration over chunks array.
Line 159: const res = await api.googleOrganicTaskPost(tasks) — awaited serially inside loop.
CHUNK_SIZE=100 (line 34); 210 queries / 100 = 3 chunks = 3 sequential POST round trips.

residual_risks: Poll tick wall time can overshoot pollCeilingMs (line 180) by the full duration of the serial taskGetAdvanced loop within a single tick. The while-condition is checked at loop-top only; a tick that starts just before the ceiling can run 42s of serial fetches past it.
Parallelizing taskGetAdvanced without a concurrency limit risks DataForSEO rate limiting (HTTP 429). Any parallel implementation should use p-limit or equivalent at <=20 concurrency.
testing_gaps: No test that measures or bounds wall-time for a full-size run (DATAFORSEO_MAX_BATCH_PER_RUN=500). Serial fetch latency is invisible to correctness tests.
No test simulating a poll tick where all tasks are ready simultaneously — the worst-case serial-fetch scenario (N=totalTasks on first tick) is untested.
